subject: Phased capacity deposit proposal to preserve rates for renewal

Subject: Renewal pricing — looking to lock rates with a phased deposit approach

Hi Stephanie / Marcus,

Hope you’re both well. We’re entering renewal season for our AI infra contract and getting a lot of internal pressure to avoid any rate increases next year. Our finance team is open to putting cash up front if that helps — we’re considering a multi-year approach but need something that matches our budget cadence.

High level we’re looking for:
- A way to lock per-token rates for 24 months (or a strong rate cap)
- The ability to spread cash commitments across two or three payment events tied to our fiscal quarters (Q3/Q1)
- A clear ramp schedule so we don’t overcommit early if usage is lower than forecast

Can Redwood propose a phased deposit / tranche structure (examples if possible) and the discount tiers you would apply at each tranche? Also include any minimums or early-exit terms we should know about.

If helpful we can jump on a 30 min call next week.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear ask, and this is exactly the kind of problem we build for. I’m looping in Marcus (AE) and Rishi (Head of Sales) to confirm commercial guardrails.

Quick summary of options we typically propose (I'll attach a worked example and term sheet):

Option A — 24-month fixed-rate prepay (single upfront):
- Upfront payment covering 24 months of committed units
- Largest discount (tiered by commitment level)
- Pros: simplest to administer, best rate certainty
- Cons: heavier near-term cash drawdown; limited flexibility on usage variance

Option B — Phased-tranche prepay (recommended to match your ask):
- Split commitment into 2–3 tranches (we usually see 60/30/10 or 50/30/20 climbs) tied to fiscal milestones
- Each tranche unlocks the next discounted rate; unused committed units convert to carry-forward credits with 12-month expiry
- Pros: preserves rate certainty while smoothing cash impact, allows mid-term course correction
- Cons: slightly lower headline discount vs single-pay prepay

Option C — Annual prepay + rollback protection:
- Prepay per-year with an agreed per-token price cap for year 2
- Lower discount than multi-year prepaid but better for customers with uncertain growth

Commercial notes we need from you: expected committed units per quarter (ballpark is fine), preferred cadence for tranche payments, and any legal constraints (e.g., Purchase Order timelines). I’ve attached a short example schedule and a draft term summary.

Next steps: Marcus, can you put together a tranche schedule using Avery’s rough numbers on file? Rishi — are the discount ranges in the attached docally within acceptable bounds or do you want a narrower set?

Available for a quick sync Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks for looping me in. Quick commercial guardrails from our side so Marcus has clear constraints when modeling scenarios: 

1) Discount bands (applied to list per-token rate):
- 1x annual prepay: up to 18% at sufficient volume
- 2-year single prepay: up to 28% at target enterprise commit
- Phased 2-year tranches: 20–24% depending on tranche timing and total commitment

2) Minimums & protections:
- Minimum effective commitment: 300k equivalent usage units/year (can be blended)
- Unused committed units convert to credits valid for 12 months; credits are non-refundable
- Early termination: prorated refund on unused prepay only if termination is customer-initiated for cause; otherwise credits retained

3) Approval path and concessions:
- Deals requesting >25% discount or unusual termination terms need direct sign-off from VP Sales (me) and Legal (cc Laura)
- For multi-year locked pricing we require a short AMPA (commercial summary) plus PO or SOW; legal turnaround 3–5 business days for standard terms

Marcus — model the phased example with both a conservative (50/30/20) and aggressive (60/30/10) tranche split. Include an option where the second tranche is conditional on meeting a minimum usage trigger to reduce overcommit risk. Add a small early-adopter credit (one-time) if Avery agrees to a 24-month lock and electronic signature within 10 business days.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Proposed tranche schedule and MAP for Avery renewal

Ben — per Stephanie and Rishi's notes, attached is a proposed tranche schedule and a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP). Summary below.

Proposed structure (example A — conservative):
- Total commitment: equivalent of $1,200,000 over 24 months
- Tranche 1 (due on signature, Q3): $600,000 (50%) — rate locked at $0.0009/token
- Tranche 2 (Q1 next fiscal): $360,000 (30%) — rate locked at $0.00095/token
- Tranche 3 (Q2 next fiscal): $240,000 (20%) — rate locked at $0.00100/token
- Unused units roll as credits for 12 months; credits apply to overages first
- One-time onboarding credit: $25k if signed within 10 business days

Alternative (example B — front-loaded): 60/30/10 with slightly deeper blended discount on tranche 1 (we can show the P&L impact in the attached spreadsheet).

MAP (condensed):
1) 7/1 — Commercial sign-off on selected tranche structure (A or B)
2) 7/5 — Legal to confirm standard terms and PO acceptance
3) 7/9 — DocuSign circulation and execution
4) 7/12 — Tranche 1 invoice issued and onboarding kickoff

Next steps: Please confirm which structure you prefer and whether Avery needs any carve-outs (e.g., data residency or audit clauses) before I route to Legal for a term sheet. I attached RDW-Termsheet-v1.docx and the spreadsheet with numbers.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Marcus / Stephanie — this looks sensible and aligns with what Finance wants to see. We prefer the conservative split (50/30/20) to keep flexibility while giving Redwood meaningful up-front coverage. A couple quick clarifications before we go to legal:

- Can the tranche 2 payment be conditioned on a 10% usage tolerance (i.e., if actual usage < 90% of forecast, tranche 2 reduces proportionally)?
- Please confirm whether credits expire exactly 12 months from issuance or end-of-quarter (we prefer EOY alignment if possible).
- Please send the term sheet into our procurement inbox and cc legal@averylabs.com; we’ll aim to review within 2 business days.

If those answers are standard, routing to DocuSign after your legal review works for us. Please provide the DocuSign URL when ready.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Ben
